title: Inqeduagent: Adaptive AI Learning Partners with Gaussian Process Augmentation
authors: Wen-Xi Yang; Tian-Fang Zhao; Guan Liu
source_name: Asia Conference on Machine Learning and Computing (ACMLC)
abstract: Collaborative partnerships play a crucial role in inquiry-oriented education. However, most learning partners are currently assigned through experience-driven heuristics or rule-based machine assistants, which often result in limited knowledge expansion and low adaptability. To address these challenges, this study introduces InqEduAgent, an LLM-empowered generative agent framework designed to simulate and select adaptive learning partners for inquiry-based learning. InqEduAgent integrates a Gaussian process-augmented matching mechanism to model the cognitive and evaluative characteristics of learners, allowing adaptive partner selection based on prior knowledge patterns. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that InqEduAgent consistently achieves superior performance across diverse learning scenarios and large language model configurations. This study advances human-AI collaborative learning by enabling intelligent pairing between human- and AI-based learning partners, and contributes to adaptive user modeling and personalized recommendation within Web-based educational environments.

title: Redefining Middle Management: How Generative AI Reshapes Roles and Competencies
authors: Philippe Jean-Baptiste
source_name: Lecture notes in networks and systems
abstract: This ongoing research investigates how Generative AI (GAI) reshapes the roles and competencies of middle managers. While most work targets macro-level impacts, we focus on micro-level changes in adaptation, decision-making, and skill reconfiguration. Using activity theory and an inductive qualitative design, we analyze 60 semi-structured interviews with middle managers from three contrasting contexts: a large energy enterprise, a medium-sized digital services firm, and a small telecommunications company. The multi-site setup enables comparison across governance models and cultures. Preliminary results show middle managers often lead GAI experimentation, initiating bottom-up innovations outside official IT channels. These shadow practices accelerate problem-solving yet create risks around data protection, compliance, and strategic drift. Beyond automating routine work, GAI supports cognitive structuring, altering how managers plan, communicate, and lead. The findings point to hybrid competencies that extend beyond technical literacy: conceptual skills (sense-making, systems thinking), human skills (empathy, leadership, conflict mediation), and ethical awareness. Middle managers emerge as pivotal translators between frontline innovation and top-down strategy. The paper contributes a multi-dimensional account of managerial transformation through the lens of activity theory and offers actionable guidance for responsible GAI integration: adaptive governance, targeted upskilling, and protected âsafe-to-experimentâ spaces. Future work will expand the dataset and trace longitudinal trajectories of adoption and governance.

title: AI-Assisted Interactive Furniture Layout Optimization for Barrier-Free Living: A Hybrid LLM-Heuristic Approach
authors: Gatla, Nikhil;Walter, Christian Felix;Rogalski, Sven
source_name: Proceedings of the International Conference on Education and Research in Computer Aided Architectural Design in Europe
abstract: Designing barrier-free indoor environments demands strict adherence to accessibility regulations while accommodating diverse room geometries and furniture configurations. Conventional rule-based layout systems address this through explicit constraint encoding yet remain inherently rigid and incapable of producing generative layout suggestions beyond their programmed boundaries. This paper investigates the integration of large language models into an accessibility-aware furniture layout optimization framework, examining their capacity to internalize regulatory compliance patterns through fine-tuning on a synthetically generated dataset. Layout planning is formulated as a constrained optimization problem grounded in DIN 18040-2 accessibility standards. The proposed hybrid system combines a fine-tuned language model operating as a generative layout proposer with a deterministic rule-based geometric validator, establishing a decision-making hierarchy between probabilistic generation and exact compliance enforcement. The system is evaluated on a set of held-out room layouts, demonstrating a 46.0% average reduction in accessibility violations across 500 held-out test layouts. The paper further engages critically with the demonstrated capabilities and limitations of this approach, including the boundaries of geometric compliance as a representation of fully barrier-free spatial experience, and discusses the broader implications for AI-assisted design under regulatory constraints.

title: Sustainable supplier selection for SMEs based on an extended PROMETHEE II approach
authors: Tong, Li Zhong; Wang, Jindan; Pu, Zhongmin
source_name: JOURNAL OF CLEANER PRODUCTION
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) play a very important role in national production, and provide more than 60% of the employment opportunities for the society. The benign development of small and medium-sized enterprises determines the sustainability of economic operation. In recent years, small and medium-sized enterprises have faced increasing operational pressure. Due to scale limitations, insufficient funds and weak bargaining power, small and medium-sized enterprises are often at a disadvantage when dealing with suppliers. One the one hand, large suppliers rely on the imbalance of bargaining power to increase the transaction costs of small and medium-sized enterprises; On the other hand, small and medium-sized suppliers with poor reputation may use legal loopholes to commit fraud, which may even threaten the survival of small and medium-sized enterprises in severe cases. However, the existing literature focuses more on the situation of large organizations facing complex and diverse suppliers. Therefore, this paper constructed a supplier selection evaluation framework for small and medium-sized enterprises, and proposed an extended PROMETHEE â¡ method to achieve sustainable supplier selection process. First, establish a sustainable supplier selection evaluation framework from the three dimensions of product and service capability, cooperation degree and risk factors; Second, combine the PROMETHEE â¡ approach with subjective preference parameters and probability language term set (PLTS) to obtain an extended PROMETHEE â¡ approach; Last, use the methodology of this paper to implement sustainable supplier selection for a small and medium-sized enterprise (M company) in China. The practical case and sensitivity analysis showed that the evaluation framework and method proposed in this paper were applicable and effective. Actual cases and sensitivity analysis showed that cost, credit and corporate irregularities were the three most important aspects for small and medium-sized enterprises to evaluate supplier performance.

Supply chain-based forecasting using artificial intelligence (AI) holds the promise to overcome these issues. This paper presents a systematic literature review of the most advanced AI approaches used in predicting supply chain disruption specific to the automotive industry. title: Speak Your Network: Automated Network Emulation Construction with Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Orchestration
authors: Zou, Daolin;Xu, Jie;Luo, Long;Yu, Hongfang
source_name: IEEE International Workshop on Quality of Service Iwqos
abstract: Network research often relies on high fidelity emulation, but constructing greenfield environments still requires substantial manual effort. LLM agents face a gap between intent and implementation: long contexts, weak validation, and uniform model use make it difficult to translate intent into working emulator state. We present Nice, a closed-loop multi-agent framework that constructs greenfield emulations from natural language intents. Nice combines a hierarchical supervisor and worker architecture with context isolation, closed-loop verification for state grounding and self-healing, dual-layer experience memory, and adaptive LLM routing. On a 30-task benchmark, Nice increases success rate from 3.3% to 90.0%, reduces average model cost from 0.045 to 0.034 per task relative to the variant without routing, and improves first pass rate from 46.7% to 76.7%.

title: Predictive GIS Modelling for Renewable Energy Site Suitability Using LLM Reasoning Pipelines
authors: Dawar, Dhruv;Khandpur, Shivya;Roychowdhury, Sneha;Sharma, Arun;Jha, Deeptanshu
source_name: Proceedings 2025 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology Aist 2025
abstract: India has shown a strong inclination towards renewable energy transformation, setting goals for 500 GW of renewable capacity by 2030 and net-zero carbon emissions by 2070. However, site planning for renewable energy faces significant challenges, requiring precise selection with regulatory and environmental constraints in a country where a large number of stakeholders lack technical domain expertise. In order to address these challenges, this study presents GeoSolarX: A geospatial intelligence framework with a conversational interface. Our key offering is a unique hybrid AI-GIS architecture with template-guided Chain-of-Thought (CoT) planner. This is powered by a large language model with fixed fusion weights and deterministic GIS operations. Current Geographic Information System (GIS) workflows are rigid and rely on the technical expertise of the user, often being complex and resource intensive. Our proposal seeks to improve interpretability and cross-modal alignment by offering weighted fusion modeling over five complementary modalities: Imagery, Tabular Attributes, Textual Context, Time-Series Data, and Graph Structure. Our framework integrates Large-Language Models with advanced geoprocessing tools in an effort to enable access to policymakers, planners, and rural stakeholders by employing a multilingual, voice-enabled interface to participate in decision making and spatial analysis without requiring GIS expertise.

title: Knowledge-Informed Primary School Layout Planning via RAG-Based Multimodal LLMs
authors: Weishi Zhou; Lu Gao; Minglai Chen; Xin Song Li; Pengpeng Liang; Gen Yang; Jiang Wen; Zhenshan Jin

abstract: Automated architectural layout planning for primary school campuses presents a highly constrained optimization challenge, requiring simultaneous adherence to functional zoning principles and national regulatory standards. Existing GAN-based approaches operate at the pixel level and frequently produce layouts that are visually coherent yet functionally deficient-a limitation we term semantic blindness. To address this gap, we propose a Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhanced Multimodal Large Language Model (RAG-MLLM) framework that grounds generation in structured domain knowledge. The framework encodes the Code for Design of Schools (GB 50099-2011) into a FAISS-indexed vector store of 87 regulatory clauses, dynamically retrieved at inference time and injected into a threelayer promptâcomprising Role, Task, and Constraint componentsâsubmitted to Gemini 3.1 Flash Image for cross-modal spatial reasoning. Experiments on the Open SCUT-AutoALP dataset show that a double-blind expert evaluation confirms a 33.4% improvement in Functional Completeness and a 7.7% gain in Spatial Rationality over the Pix2PixHD baseline, with distributional analysis further corroborating closer alignment to professional design norms. These results demonstrate the potential of knowledge-driven generation for regulation-critical architectural typologies.

title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning
authors: DÃ­dac SurÃ­s; Sachit Menon; Carl Vondrick
abstract: Answering visual queries is a complex task that requires both visual processing and reasoning. End-to-end models, the dominant approach for this task, do not explicitly differentiate between the two, limiting interpretability and generalization. Learning modular programs presents a promising alternative, but has proven challenging due to the difficulty of learning both the programs and modules simultaneously. We introduce ${\color{green}{\text{ViperGPT}}}$, a framework that leverages code-generation models to compose vision-and-language models into subroutines to produce a result for any query. ${\color{green}{\text{ViperGPT}}}$ utilizes a provided API to access the available modules, and composes them by generating Python code that is later executed. This simple approach requires no further training, and achieves state-of-the-art results across various complex visual tasks.

title: Backdoor Adjustment of Confounding by Provenance for Robust Text Classification of Multi-institutional Clinical Notes
authors: Ding, Xiruo;Sheng, Zhecheng;YetiÅgen, Meliha;Pakhomov, Serguei;Cohen, Trevor
source_name: AMIA Annual Symposium Proceedings AMIA Symposium
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods have been broadly applied to clinical tasks. Machine learning and deep learning approaches have been used to improve the performance of clinical NLP. However, these approaches require sufficiently large datasets for training, and trained models have been shown to transfer poorly across sites. These issues have led to the promotion of data collection and integration across different institutions for accurate and portable models. However, this can introduce a form of bias called confounding by provenance. When source-specific data distributions differ at deployment, this may harm model performance. To address this issue, we evaluate the utility of backdoor adjustment for text classification in a multi-site dataset of clinical notes annotated for mentions of substance abuse. Using an evaluation framework devised to measure robustness to distributional shifts, we assess the utility of backdoor adjustment. Our results indicate that backdoor adjustment can effectively mitigate for confounding shift.
